Ingredients:

  • 6-7 dl of berries (blueberries, red currants or black currants)
  • 250 g of brown sugar
  • 250 g of regular sugar
  • 4 liters of water
  • 1/5 teaspoons of yeast (I used 1/4 teaspoons of dry yeast instead)
  • +
  • little bit of sugar and few raisins for each bottle

Instructions:

  1. Smash the berries slighty
  2. Boil 1 liter of water. Add the berries and sugars. Let it boil. Pour it in a 10 liter plastic bucket. Add 3 liters of cold water
  3. Let it cool down to hand temperature (I used dry yeast so made it little bit hotter 42 °C) and mix in the yeast. Let the bucket be in room temperature for a day
  4. Strain the liquid in clean bottles. Add a teaspoon of sugar and few raisins in each bottle. Refrigerate the bottles. After few days the raisins will rise to the top and that will indicate that sima is ready for drinking.

Pressure rises during fermenting, so don't use too tight cork. Keep refrigerated and sima will last for a week or so.

When making sima, you can use just plain sugar, in which case you will get lighter color and milder taste. Or mix in all sorts of sugars - plain old white sugar, brown sugar, syrup or honey.
